title: From laboratory signal to policy-ready claim
subtitle: A toy uncertainty map for testing temporal DAG layout
concept: Structure uncertainty without prematurely resolving it.

nodes.title: Lab assay shows target effect
nodes.summary: A controlled laboratory assay reports the target effect under narrow conditions.
nodes.audit_note: This supports a lab-scoped claim, not deployment, clinical, industrial, legal, or policy readiness.

nodes.title: Effect exists under narrow lab conditions
nodes.summary: It is reasonable to treat the laboratory signal as a scoped working hypothesis.
nodes.falsification_condition: Independent replication under the same protocol fails to reproduce the effect.
nodes.audit_note: This is a bounded claim: lab effect, not real-world usefulness.

nodes.title: Independent replication partly succeeds
nodes.summary: A second team observes a weaker but directionally similar effect.
nodes.audit_note: Replication raises confidence in the lab signal while preserving uncertainty about magnitude.

nodes.title: The effect may survive scale-up
nodes.summary: A scale-up hypothesis can be explored, but it remains unresolved.
nodes.falsification_condition: Pilot-scale testing fails to preserve effect size, cost, safety, or energy balance.
nodes.audit_note: This is a frontier claim: plausible enough to test, too weak to treat as established.

nodes.title: Pilot test loses most of the effect
nodes.summary: A pilot test reports lower effect size and higher operational cost outside the laboratory setting.
nodes.audit_note: This later evidence weakens the earlier scale-up hypothesis.

nodes.title: Net energy balance unresolved
nodes.summary: The total system-level energy balance is not yet known.
nodes.falsification_condition: Full lifecycle accounting shows the process is net negative under realistic operating conditions.
nodes.audit_note: Unknowns remain first-class nodes rather than hidden caveats.

nodes.title: Readiness narrative
nodes.summary: A public-facing frame treats the technique as nearly ready for broad use.
nodes.audit_note: Narrative pressure can outrun source-local evidence.

nodes.title: Policy-ready deployment claim
nodes.summary: The strong claim says the technique is ready for policy mandate or real-world deployment.
nodes.falsification_condition: Pilot-scale or lifecycle evaluation fails under realistic deployment constraints.
nodes.audit_note: This is parked as an overclaim because lab evidence and public narrative do not establish deployment readiness.

nodes.title: Required limiting tests
nodes.summary: Pilot replication, lifecycle accounting, safety testing, and cost sensitivity are needed before the strong claim can move upward.
nodes.audit_note: A claim should say what would weaken it before presenting itself as credible.

edges.rationale: Older lab evidence supports a later lab-scoped hypothesis.
Later replication audits and strengthens the earlier scoped claim.
A bounded lab signal motivates, but does not prove, scale-up.
Later pilot evidence weakens the earlier scale-up hypothesis.
Unresolved system-level energy balance blocks policy readiness.
A public readiness frame pressures the claim upward without adding direct evidence.
Pilot-scale weakness directly undermines a deployment-ready claim.
Required limiting tests define what must be checked before the claim can be upgraded.
